Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

total adjective

complete, utter: total silence, total nonsense

also utter, sheer, absolute

classical

Cic. Agr. 1.21: summa tranquillitās pācis et ōtiī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 44: ex summā inopiā (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 4.17: summa difficultās

summus, summa, summum

adjective (superlative of superus), declension

utmost, total, complete (of degree)

The highest degree of anything: total calm, total want, the greatest difficulty.

Other words

  • merus, mera, merum — sheer, nothing but, pure

    adjective, declension · classical · Cic. Att. 1.18.1: sōlitūdō mera; Cic. Att. 9.13.8: merum bellum loquitur

    Properly unmixed, as wine without water (merum); then “nothing but”: mera mōnstra nūntiārat, he had brought nothing but horrors (Cic. Att. 4.7.1).

  • tōtus, tōta, tōtum — whole, entire; utter

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 401

    Traupman’s word for “utter”: tōtus is “the whole of”, and stands for “utter” only where the whole of something is meant.

Examples

  • nōn homō sed lītus atque āēr et sōlitūdō mera

    (of a man who was no company) not a man but a seashore, thin air, utter emptinessCic. Att. 1.18.1

  • tanta repente vīlitās ex summā inopiā et cāritāte reī frūmentāriae cōnsecūta est

    so sudden a fall in prices followed upon total scarcity and the dearness of grainCic. Imp. Pomp. 44

See also total, whole, nonsense!.
